memories.memory: I usually vote for candidates who support strong public schools, accessible health care, and practical investments in local infrastructure, even when they are not from the party I normally favor.
After thirty years in public-sector work, I have become firmly convinced that government programs should be judged by measurable results rather than by slogans or loyalty to a political party.
I attend a small United Methodist church twice a month, and my faith has made me more patient with people whose political views are very different from mine.
I was raised to believe that a person should leave public institutions more capable and trustworthy than they found them, which is why I still volunteer for civic projects after retirement.
I support expanding legal protections for same-sex couples and transgender adults, although I sometimes avoid discussing those views with relatives who see the issue very differently.
I am troubled by how quickly political arguments have become personal, and I stopped sharing political posts on social media after a disagreement with a former colleague in October 2023.
My private political priority for the next decade is reducing corruption and undue influence in government, including stricter disclosure rules for contractors and campaign donors.
